title: Abhyankar residue separability for a local DVR compositum diagram
statement: Let B,A,U,T be DVR domains [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], with a finite faithful B-algebra A [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], a local B-algebra U, and a local A-algebra T. Let n>0 and e be natural numbers with e a unit in B and e dividing n. Suppose m_B A=m_A^n and m_B U=m_U^e. Write k(V)=V/m_V for the residue field of a local ring V, and assume k(U)/k(B) is separable [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. Let E be a finite separable extension of Frac(B) [def-pc-field-extension] with compatible B-algebra structure. Give E a U-algebra structure making E the fraction field of U, compatibly with B. Let F be a field, an A-algebra, and i:E->F a ring homomorphism such that i(b)=b for b in B, through the specified maps. Assume F is generated as an A-algebra by i(E). Give F a T-algebra structure making F the fraction field of T, compatibly with A. Suppose j:U->T is local, agrees on B with B->A->T, and its composite U->T->F equals U->E->F. Then the induced extension k(T)/k(A) is separable.

source.place: Tags 0BRM (Abhyankar lemma), 09EM (normalization diagrams), and 09E7 (adic smoothness criterion).

proof.text: Identify A with the integral closure of B in Frac(A), by finiteness, faithfulness, and normality. The ideal identities express the two ramification indices as n and e. The compatible fraction-field maps and generation identify F with a field factor of E tensor over Frac(B) with Frac(A).

The local map j selects the corresponding valuation ring in F. An integrally closed DVR containing the normalization localized at its center equals that localization, since any proper overring of a DVR in the same fraction field is its fraction field. This identifies T with the local normalized compositum in Stacks 09EM.

Follow the root calculation of Stacks 0BRM: write a uniformizer of B as a unit times an n-th power of a uniformizer of A. Adjoin an e-th root of that unit by a finite etale extension, reducing to a base field containing an e-th root of the uniformizer of B. Descend along this finite etale extension after the calculation.

Since e divides n, the base change factors through the standard uniformizer-root extension. In this root case dividing the base root by a uniformizer of U adjoins an e-th root of a unit, so the resulting extension over U is finite etale. Multiplicativity of ramification indices gives index one over the root base; residue separability follows by transitivity, because k(U)/k(B) is separable. The arbitrary further base change is handled by Stacks 09EQ, as in 0BRM.
The preceding calculation and descent give maximal-ideal-adic formal smoothness of A->T. Apply Stacks 09E7 to obtain the asserted separability for the given local residue-field algebra.
